validity.recommendation: No action — existence, classification, and non-duplicate status are all solid.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: unambiguously real and one of the best-documented Kazakh trunk gas pipelines. JV 'Beineu-Shymkent Gas Pipeline LLP' formed by KazTransGas + Trans-Asia Gas Pipeline Co Ltd (CNODC/CNPC subsidiary); construction financed by $1.8bn CDB/Bank of China syndicated loan (Phase I) plus a further $700M for Phase II (China AidData project #39562/#40362/#73384); phased commissioning 2013/2015/2016/2018/2019 (bsgp.kz 'About us' page); continuously in the news through 2023-2025 re: a proposed second line/expansion (Sputnik KZ 2023, Kursiv 2024/2025, Inbusiness.kz 2024). OSM independently carries a named, unmatched-to-anything-else trace of 1,443.6 km that the reconciliation engine auto-attributed to this exact PID (location + rough-length corroboration only, per project convention, but it is another origin agreeing this pipe is where GEM says it is). CLASSIFICATION: KazMunayGas Annual Report 2021 (ar2021.kmg.kz PDF) explicitly labels it 'TRUNK GAS PIPELINE BEINEU-BOZOI-SHYMKENT' in its own infrastructure map/table -> PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas are both correct, not a gathering/feeder line. DUPLICATE: name and PID are unique in the 39-row Kazakhstan-gas roster; no other row in scope represents this physical pipe. Its long-discussed 'second line' (2.7 trillion tenge estimate, Kursiv 2024-02-23) is a distinct, not-yet-built expansion project tracked separately and is not in this batch, so it is not a duplicate risk for the existing operating P3273.

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's current Operator value, 'Intergas Central Asia', is wrong for this specific pipeline. Two independent primary sources establish the true operator: (1) bsgp.kz's own 'About us' page: 'The pipeline is operated by Beineu-Shymkent Gas Pipeline LLP, established in December 2010 ... a joint venture with equal participation from Kazakhstan and China: KazTransGas JSC ... [and] Trans-Asia Gas Pipeline (a subsidiary of CNPC).' (2) KazMunayGas Annual Report 2021 (ar2021.kmg.kz PDF, 'Gas Transportation and Marketing' section) carries an explicit 'Management company' table with FOUR separate columns — JSC Intergas Central Asia (ICA) | Asia Gas Pipeline LLP | Beineu-Shymkent Gas Pipeline LLP | JSC KazTransGas Aimak — each with its own routes/length/capacity. ICA's column covers 15,260 km of DIFFERENT routes ('Kazakhstan, Russia, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan', 198 bcm/y capacity — i.e. the CAC, Bukhara-Ural, Makat-N.Caucasus, Soyuz/Orenburg-Novopskov, Okarem-Beyneu family), while Beineu-Shymkent Gas Pipeline LLP is its own column at 1,454 km / 15 bcm/y — exactly this pipeline. The same table (and the accompanying map graphic, verified via pdftotext -layout since it's a large PDF the substring checker under-reads) explicitly labels the route 'TRUNK GAS PIPELINE BEINEU-BOZOI-SHYMKENT' next to its own 'INTERGAS CENTRAL ASIA / ASIA GAS PIPELINE / BEINEU-SHYMKENT GAS PIPELINE' management-company box, i.e. Beineu-Shymkent Gas Pipeline is listed as its own management entity, distinct from ICA, in the very same graphic. So Operator='Intergas Central Asia' is a real (not GEM-only) but MISPLACED value — it belongs to a different family of Kazakh trunk lines, not to P3273. Owner1/Owner2 on the sheet (QazaqGaz 50% / Trans-Asia Gas Pipeline Co Ltd 50%, ref bsgp.kz) are correct and consistent with this finding — only the separate Operator field is wrong.

validity.researcher_notes: SPEC — every numeric field checked out. LENGTH: bsgp.kz's own 'About us' page states 'the actual length of BBS is 1 449,503km' — matches GEM's LengthKnown=1449.00 km to within rounding. KMG AR2021 independently states 'the length of the Beineu-Shymkent gas pipeline is 1,454 km' — a different KZ corporate source, 0.3% higher, immaterial (likely a slightly different route/lateral-inclusion basis, not a data error). DIAMETER: 1067mm (=42in) confirmed by TWO independent sources — bsgp.kz ('the pipe diameter 1067mm') and the pipeline's own EPC contractor kazstroyservice.com project page ('размер трубы/протяженность: Д 1067 mm'). CAPACITY: 15.00 bcm/y is confirmed as the pipeline's DESIGN/target capacity by KMG AR2021 ('its capacity is 15 bln m3 per year') and by bsgp.kz ('planned to expand the Gas Pipeline capacities up to 15 bln.m3'). Caveat worth recording: bsgp.kz also states its CURRENT actual throughput at the time of writing was only 13 bln.m3/year — GEM's Capacity field is tracking nameplate/design capacity (consistent with how this field is used elsewhere in the Kazakh roster), not current utilization; not a defect, just worth noting for context. START YEAR: StartYear1=2013 confirmed by bsgp.kz ('In December 2013 linear part and Bozoy GMS of the Gas Pipeline ... were commissioned') consistent with Order 350 para 165 (commissioned 2013 at 10 bcm/y design, per the orchestrator's earlier read of that order's prose). LOCATION: Beyneu/Mangystau Region start and Shymkent/Turkistan Region end both confirmed by bsgp.kz prose. The existing Location [ref] (https://adilet.zan.kz/files/1486/69/2.jpg, a map JPG) shows a timeout in the worklist's automated check — manually re-verified LIVE (HTTP 200 via curl, twice) — it is NOT dead, no ref change needed, this was a transient network hiccup on the automated pass. Status=operating is overwhelmingly confirmed independent of the Order-350 text-match failure (launch coverage 2015, 'reached design capacity' 2020, ongoing second-line planning news through 2025).

fills.researcher_notes: bsgp.kz: the JV 'Beineu-Shymkent Gas Pipeline LLP' — the project company — 'was established' in December 2010. AidData's record of the underlying agreement dates the joint venture's actual establishment to January 18, 2011. The two sources straddle the December-2010/January-2011 turn but agree the project was formally proposed/launched right around 2011, consistent with GEM's ProposalYear=2011; not treating the one-month spread as a discrepancy given both are describing the same JV-formation event.

Samruk-Kazyna (KZ sovereign wealth fund, parent of KMG/KazTransGas) press release dated the day after the event: 'накануне в Туркестане состоялась торжественная церемония сварки первого стыка линейной части газопровода Бейнеу-Бозой-Шымкент' — the welding ceremony for the pipeline's first joint, in Turkestan, September 2011. Kazinform's own historical-dates calendar independently corroborates the year: '3 года назад (2011) в Туркестане состоялась церемония сварки первого стыка...'. Two independent state/news organizations, same year -> ConstructionYear=2011 confirmed.

fills.primary_value: West Kazakhstan oil and gas fields
fills.researcher_notes: CAVEAT — this is only a partial match, staged as best-effort per instructions rather than left blank. bsgp.kz names two specific West Kazakhstan (Aktobe Region) fields, Urikhtau and Zhanazhol, as gas sources — but only 'in particular for the export of natural gas to China' via a planned capacity expansion, not as the base/original supply. KMG AR2021 gives the pipeline's original stated purpose as 'facilitate the transit of Turkmen and Uzbek gas to China, exports of Kazakh gas to China, as well as uninterrupted gas supply to southern regions of Kazakhstan' — i.e. its base gas is largely Central-Asian import/transit gas entering at Beineu (from the CAC system), not solely West Kazakh field gas. 'West Kazakhstan oil and gas fields' is directionally correct (Urikhtau/Zhanazhol are genuinely West Kazakh fields feeding this system) but is an incomplete picture of the supply mix. Tier kept low / single source; flagging the nuance rather than asserting a clean match.

Intergas Central Asia's own 2015-08-21 news item on the syndicated construction loan states directly: 'Стоимость проекта строительства МГ "ББШ" составляет $3,6 млрд.' — an exact match to GEM's SegmentCost=$3.6bn. This is the same primary source the gem.wiki page itself footnotes for this figure (footnote 12) — verified independently here by reading the page directly rather than trusting the wiki citation, per SOP. Single strong primary source (the pipeline company's own press release with a specific figure) -> tier medium; did not find a second fully independent outlet repeating the exact $3.6bn figure (a February-2024 Kursiv/Minenergo cost estimate found in search is for the unrelated, not-yet-built second line at 2.7 trillion tenge, not this value).

summary: P3273 (Beineu-Bozoy-Shymkent, operating) is real, correctly classified, and not a duplicate; length/diameter/capacity/dates all independently corroborated (bsgp.kz operator site + KMG AR2021 + EPC contractor page), with four MISSING_REF cells now filled (Proposal 2011, Construction 2011, SegmentCost $3.6bn all solid; FuelSource staged low-tier with a caveat). One real defect found: Operator='Intergas Central Asia' is WRONG — should be 'Beineu-Shymkent Gas Pipeline LLP', confirmed by two independent primary sources (bsgp.kz + KMG AR2021's own management-company table, which lists the two as separate entities with separate route portfolios) — routed to Update, not filled with the current value.
